item.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE
item.description: A China-linked group chained a Chrome renderer bug with a Windows privilege-escalation zero-day to drop the GRIMWEDGE backdoor, showing browser and OS patches need to move in lockstep.

item.title: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
item.description: A single unauthenticated RCE in the Marimo notebook server let a real attacker pivot to an internal SSH bastion in under ten seconds, a stark example of how thin segmentation collapses under live exploitation.

item.title: Talking to the Airgap: Exploiting Radio-Less Embedded Devices as Radio Receivers
item.description: New research shows embedded devices with no radio hardware can still be coerced into acting as ad-hoc radio receivers, undermining a common air-gap security assumption.

item.title: Valve considered making a new VR game for the Steam Frame, before tackling the "ludicrous" task of getting Half-Life: Alyx running standalone
item.description: A rare look inside Valve's effort to strip a AAA VR game free of SteamVR to run natively on standalone hardware.

item.title: Wardogs delivers what Battlefield 6 was too console-brained to pull off: A real server browser
item.description: Wardogs shipped the filterable server browser Battlefield 6 skipped, and players are already crediting it with a healthier community.

item.title: Mitotic chromosomes may assemble from pre-existing chromatin 'building blocks' during cell division
item.description: Problem: How does a cell compress ~2m of DNA into a tidy mitotic chromosome each division? Approach: Researchers synthesized decades of chromosome-scaffold and condensin research, modeling chromatin as pre-built blocks, not a blank strand folded from scratch. Result: Mitotic chromosomes seem to assemble from condensed chromatin domains already present in interphase nuclei, which condensins gather and reorganize into the familiar rod shape. Why it matters: Treating interphase and mitotic chromatin as one continuous structure reframes how cells ensure accurate chromosome handoff, with implications for genetic instability and disease. Glossary: Chromatin - DNA packaged with proteins. Condensin - complex that compacts chromosomes. Interphase - part of the cycle between divisions. Mitotic chromosome - coiled structure seen during division.

item.title: Disordered atoms steer shared light pulses by matching motion and timing
item.description: Physicists found disordered atomic ensembles can synchronize to collectively steer a shared light pulse, a step toward using messy, uncooled atomic systems for photonic control.

item.title: We got admin access to Baseten's production GitHub in 25 minutes
item.description: A red-team writeup on how a leaked GitHub PAT plus an overly broad app-to-repo trust chain gave researchers admin on Baseten's production GitHub, a clean case study in credential blast radius.

item.title: Building a Linux GPU Driver for the M4 Mac Mini in One Month
item.description: One engineer reverse-engineered enough of Apple's M4 GPU to write a from-scratch Linux driver in a month, documenting the process end to end.

item.title: Running Linux 6.11 on the ESP32-S3 with a Few Tweaks
item.description: Problem: The ESP32-S3 microcontroller has no memory management unit (MMU), hardware Linux normally needs for virtual memory and process isolation. Approach: Developer Paulneja built a NOMMU Linux config with a custom fork(), running Linux on one CPU core while the other handles WiFi/Bluetooth under FreeRTOS. Result: Version 0.8 boots reliably with 3.7MB usable RAM on a board with 16MB flash and 8MB octal PSRAM, up from the prior release. Why it matters: Minimal Linux on a cheap chip opens the door to embedded routers running BusyBox instead of a bespoke RTOS. Glossary: MMU - manages virtual memory/isolation. NOMMU - Linux variant for chips without one. PSRAM - pseudo-static RAM, denser but slower than SRAM. FreeRTOS - lightweight real-time OS.
